_comment: Verbatim /State reads from three real appliances on one household LAN,
captured 2026-08-22, each paired with what Home Assistant's *cloud* Miele
integration reported for the same appliance at the same moment. That pairing
is what identifies RemoteEnable[2] as the cloud's remoteEnable.mobileStart.
Field order is as returned. Nothing is synthesised.
The DOP2 GLOBAL_USER_REQ leaf (2/1583) was read at the same moment:
404 on both EK057 FW 08.37 devices, 200 on the EK037 FW 04.05 dryer.
That asymmetry is why write_process_action tries /State first and only
falls back to DOP2 - on these two appliances DOP2 is not an option at all.
The washer capture is the cautionary one: Status 4 with a delay start
running and RemoteEnable[2] == 0. A ProcessAction 1 written to it was
accepted and had no effect. Status 4 alone does not mean startable.
Status 4 with RemoteEnable[2] == 1. The cloud's history shows that window
existing (mobileStart flipped on exactly as the dishwasher entered
WAITING_TO_START on 2026-08-20) but miele_lan was not installed yet.
The armed dishwasher capture is the one that pins the gate. It is armed
(RemoteEnable[2] == 1) *and* counting down a delay start, simultaneously.
A gate that vetoed on StartTime would refuse exactly the case SmartStart
automations depend on - overriding a queued delay when solar is good.
Two independent appliances have now had ProcessAction 1 accepted and ignored,
both at Status 4 with the mobile-start bit at 0: the washer on a plain delay
and the dryer on a plain delay while its panel advertised 'RemoteStart
possible'. Status 4 does not mean startable; the bit does.
Pause is not universal. A TWL780WP running Cool air accepted ProcessAction 3
with 200 [{'Success':...}] and stayed in_use; the cloud integration's own
pause button for that dryer has been permanently unavailable across every
cycle it ran that day, so Miele's /actions list does not include pause for
the model at all. Stop on the same appliance moved it in_use -> 9 within
~2.5s, over /State, with no DOP2 fallback. Capability is per-model and the
LAN cannot enumerate it, which is why presses are verified rather than
trusted.
are verified rather than pre-judged.
The two dishwasher captures are the pair that solved it: same Status, same
RemoteEnable, same ProgramType - one start refused, one accepted. StandbyState
is the difference (2 vs 1), and a controlled A/B on the sleeping appliance
confirmed cause rather than correlation. start_program() now wakes first.
Reads do NOT wake these appliances or reset the idle timer: StandbyState held
at 2 across eight reads during the control arm, and they sit in deep standby
for hours while the integration polls every 60s.

dishwasher_g7369._note: mid-cycle: Status 5 (in_use). HA's cloud integration reported binary_sensor.dishwasher_mobile_start = on across this whole window (20:14:32-21:35:47 local), the only positive RemoteEnable[2] capture we have.

washer_wwi860._note: Status 4 (waiting_to_start) but on a 10h29m DELAY START, not armed for remote start. ProcessAction 1 was accepted here (200, no Failure) and ignored - still Status 4 twenty seconds later. StartTime is what tells the two Status-4 situations apart.

dryer_twl780wp._note: program selected but not armed: Status 3 (programmed), door open

dishwasher_g7369_armed._note: ARMED but ASLEEP - StandbyState 2. ProcessAction 1 written here is acknowledged 200 [{'Success':...}] and ignored. Confirmed as cause, not correlation, by a controlled A/B minutes apart on this appliance in this exact state: no-wake refused, wake-then-write started it in two seconds. Compare dishwasher_g7369_started_ok.
dishwasher_g7369_armed._programtype_note: backfilled from recorder history; this unit only ever reports 0

dryer_twl780wp_delay_not_armed._note: The trap this gate exists for. Panel read 'Cool Air, Start In 5h, RemoteStart possible' - so the appliance itself advertises remote start - yet the mobile-start bit is 0 because it is counting down a plain delay timer rather than waiting on the network. ProcessAction 1 written here answered 200 [{'Success':...}] and the machine did not move: Status 4 for 24s, StartTime frozen. 'RemoteStart possible' on the panel is the capability, not the arming.

dishwasher_g7369_started_ok._note: The one that WORKED. Captured immediately before a successful remote start: /State ProcessAction 1 took it Status 4 -> 5 in two seconds and zeroed StartTime, on firmware that 404s every DOP2 leaf and does not even advertise the resource. Compare dishwasher_g7369_armed, which failed: same appliance, same Status, same RemoteEnable, same ProgramType. The fields that differ are ProgramPhase (1792 vs 0) and StandbyState (1 vs 2, deep standby). Not yet enough to gate on.
